question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
**Yes.** In the latest CPI data (August 2026), electricity prices were up **13.2%** year-on-year, against **4.0%** for all groups.

Electricity has been running well ahead of headline inflation since mid-2025:

| Period | Electricity (y/y) | All groups (y/y) |
|---|---|---|
| Jun 2025 | -6.3% | 1.9% |
| Oct 2025 | 37.1% | 3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | 37.0% | 3.7% |
| Mar 2026 | 25.4% | 4.6% |
| Jun 2026 | 22.4% | 3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | 6.1% | 3.5% |
| Aug 2026 | 13.2% | 4.0% |

Some points on reading this:

- **The swings are partly base effects.** Electricity prices fell sharply from mid-2024 to mid-2025, so the annual rate was deeply negative (down to -35.6% in Oct 2024). It then rebounded when those year-earlier declines dropped out of the comparison. The July 2026 dip to 6.1% and the rebound to 13.2% in August are likely similar timing effects, though I haven't verified the specific causes.
- **The headline effect is smaller than the rate suggests.** Electricity has a modest weight in the CPI basket, so a 13% rise adds less to headline inflation than, say, a 13% rise in rents would.
- **The gap has narrowed from its peak.** The electricity rate was above 35% in late 2025 and early 2026, and has since come down to the low-to-mid teens, while headline inflation has stayed around 3.5–4.6%.
